title: Nearby 2004 P02 water mixtures fail the 2022 oxygen and phosphate test on density 26.6; distant mixtures fit
abstract: We test whether 2022 P02 waters at 28-32 N and 180-160 W can be mixtures of observed 2004 waters without added oxygen use. Linear programs use nonnegative source weights and temperature, salinity, oxygen and phosphate tolerances. On sigma0 26.6, sources within 10 degrees longitude match temperature and salinity for 19 of 32 cast targets but all four properties for none under nominal tolerances. The whole section fits all four for 31 of 32. On 26.5, the whole section fits all 32. Donors within 0.1 density of each target fit 26 and 21 targets at full-section radius, but these failures disappear with a wider calibration allowance. That allowance permits only 1 of 32 joint fits within 10 degrees on 26.6. The evidence rejects the tested nearby unchanged-source mixture model for most targets. It does not select ventilation loss, greater respiration or distant source changes. Broad-pool fits give a direct mixing alternative to a within-type oxygen loss inferred by local regression extrapolation. Source coverage, approximate tracer conservation, independent target weights, calibration and bottle gaps limit this conditional test.

display.caption: Joint mixture feasibility increases with the permitted source radius. Solid lines use nominal tolerances. Dotted lines use a wider oxygen and phosphate allowance. These are conditional feasibility counts, not source fraction estimates.

citations.reason: Parser and exact source versions; its local salinity support failure motivates this test.
